name: TimePicker
description: A styled native <input type="time"> that integrates with the Traxion Design System. Uses the browser's built-in time picker controls (keyboard increment/decrement, scroll wheel, AM/PM per system locale). Step is fixed at 60 seconds (1-minute precision, no seconds). Extends all standard HTML input attributes except type. For combined date and time selection in a single popover, use DateTimePicker instead.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled time value in HH:mm format (24-hour). Passed directly to the native input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Standard input onChange handler. Access the selected time via e.target.value (HH:mm string).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the input. Shows reduced opacity and a not-allowed cursor.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes merged with the base input styles via cn().

props.name: id
props.description: HTML id attribute. Use to associate the input with a Label via htmlFor.

accessibility.role: Renders as a native <input type="time"> element. The browser provides the accessible name via aria-label or an associated <label> element.
accessibility.keyboard: Tab to focus. Arrow Up/Down increment or decrement hours/minutes. The browser handles all native time input keyboard interactions including AM/PM toggling.
accessibility.aria: Associate with a Label using htmlFor/id for a proper accessible name. The native input is recognized by screen readers as a time input.
accessibility.notes: The native browser time picker UI varies between operating systems and browsers. The webkit calendar picker indicator is hidden via CSS to keep a consistent appearance.

do: Always pair with a Label using htmlFor/id: <Label htmlFor="hora">Hora</Label><TimePicker id="hora" />
Use DateTimePicker when the user needs to select both a date and a time in the same interaction.
Control width from the parent container — the input is w-full by default.
dont: Do not use TimePicker when date selection is also needed — use DateTimePicker instead.
Do not try to display seconds — the step is fixed at 60s (1 minute precision).
